title.en: Whole Body, Mobilised in Three Seconds

text.zh: 吓一跳的那一瞬间，全身十几个器官几乎同时改变了工作状态。神经来不及一个个通知——它用的是另一套办法。
text.en: In the instant you get a fright, a dozen organs change what they are doing almost at once. There is no time to notify each one separately, so the body uses another method.

text.zh: 办法就在这两顶扣在肾上的小帽子里。它们不发信号，它们往血里直接倒药——药随血走，几秒钟内到达每一个角落。
text.en: The method lives in these two small caps perched on the kidneys. They send no signal; they tip a drug straight into the blood, and the blood carries it into every corner within seconds.

text.zh: 第一个响应的是泵。跳得更快、每一下也更用力，几秒之内送出去的血量能翻上一倍还多。
text.en: The pump answers first. Faster beats, and harder ones: within seconds it can push out more than twice the blood it was moving a moment ago.

text.zh: 同时气道也松开了。管壁上的平滑肌一放松，通道变宽，同样一口气能吸进更多——供得上血，也得供得上氧。
text.en: At the same time the airways let go. The smooth muscle in their walls relaxes, the channels widen, and the same breath brings in more air — no use moving blood faster if there is nothing in it.

text.zh: 燃料也得跟上。肝把囤着的糖拆开放进血里，肌肉一伸手就能拿到——这一步决定了你能撑多久。
text.en: Fuel has to keep up too. The liver breaks open its stores of sugar and releases them into the blood, ready for muscle to grab — this is the step that decides how long you can keep going.

text.zh: 与此同时，最外面这一层的血管收紧，把血让给肌肉。脸色发白、手脚发凉，都是同一道命令的另一面。
text.en: Meanwhile the vessels in the outermost layer clamp down, surrendering their share to muscle. A pale face and cold hands are the other side of the very same order.

text.zh: 所以"吓出一身冷汗"不是比喻。一次化学广播，同时改写了泵、气道、燃料和外壳四件事——而你只感觉到心跳。
text.en: So the cold sweat of a scare is not a figure of speech. One chemical broadcast rewrites the pump, the airways, the fuel supply and the outer shell at once — and all you notice is your heartbeat.
